Alex.confusing: The Owl and Eagle visit rules were hard to pin down, especially who gains eggs from a visit and whether the visited player or the visitor is paid. Several players, including me, misread them mid-day.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when I was the Sphinx, I cast cover claims while Farm players argued over the Eagle and Owl egg counts. Nobody could tell what was true, which made the debate tense.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports show who visited whom, or at least state which egg came from which visit, so players can check claims without guessing.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw at Ellis, a Farm Kookaburra, because I trusted the egg-count argument, and that handed Meowfia the win. I would have looked harder at Casey, the Mouser who had been voting with the group, before pushing the vote.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle and Owl visit-counting was hard to track, because the dawn reports only show who visited and not which egg came from which visit. Round 2 Alex's +1 and Drew's Turkey egg got tangled in the day discussion.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when Alex's visit claim was checked against my Eagle report and the table turned on them, it felt like a real deduction game. The vote landed right.
Blair.change: I'd make it clearer in the dawn report which visitor or animal produced each egg, so players don't have to guess from counts.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw at Ellis with a Wild and called the vote on a read I hadn't verified. Knowing Ellis was actually Farm, I'd have held back and asked Casey and Drew for their visit reports before calling the vote.

Casey.confusing: The Owl's visit mechanic was hard to read: Owl lays its egg in the visited player's nest, and I initially misread who gained what, which muddied the early egg-count checks. Hugs and Eagle counts also took effort to reconcile with the dawn reports.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: Alex switched their claimed visit right after I called the vote, and Blair's Eagle count exposed the lie before the throws landed.
Casey.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who gained or lost eggs from which visit, so players can check each other's claims without guesswork.
Casey.regret: In Round 3 I threw in with the Ellis vote and took the Meowfia side's word too readily; I should have pressed harder on Drew's Tit claim, since Drew was Farm but I could have checked whether Drew's visit fit the eggs.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey payout was hard to read: I didn't know a visitor gets paid by the Turkey, so my Hawk +1 looked like a Meowfia hit. I also misread how the Owl egg is paid, which made me doubt Casey for a while.
Drew.fun: Round 1 went well: I called Blair Meowfia, then reversed once the Turkey payouts showed up, and the table still voted out Ellis, the real Floofer. Watching the egg counts explain each other was the best part.
Drew.change: Tell players what their own visitors were, or at least whether a Turkey or Eagle got paid by visitors, so the egg-count reasoning is easier to check.
Drew.regret: In Round 1 I called Blair Meowfia from a Hawk gain that was really a Turkey payout. I should have said I wasn't sure what my egg came from and asked for visit counts before accusing anyone.

Ellis.confusing: The Floofer's hug and the Owl's egg rules were hard to track, since I couldn't tell whether a hug stopped a visitor's effect or only redirected it. Blair's Turkey payout was also unclear until the table worked it out.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when the Turkey, Falcon, and Eagle egg counts lined up and we caught Alex's false visit claim from the numbers alone.
Ellis.change: I'd make the dawn reports say which egg source each gain came from, so players don't have to reverse-engineer every count during the day.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I visited Casey, a Farm Owl, which gave my Meowfia team nothing; I should have visited a player who was likely to visit me, to gain information and keep my hug useful.

Finley.confusing: The Owl and Falcon egg rules were hard to pin down from reports alone, since the Owl's egg goes to the visited player and the Turkey pays visitors, so several claims looked wrong until the mechanics clicked. Mixing up which nest gets the egg made my early read on Blair wrong.
Finley.fun: Round 1 was fun: Blair's Turkey claim and the egg counts let the table reconstruct who visited whom, and the Falcon +2 puzzle got solved in public.
Finley.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who gained eggs from which visit, so players can verify egg counts without guessing at card mechanics.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I should have thrown at Drew or stayed quiet instead of joining the Ellis vote, since Ellis was actually Farm and I helped Meowfia win by throwing my cards away. I would have checked the lost-egg claims more carefully before backing the mob.

review.title: The Wink Spoils Finley
review.headline: A lone cat winked the Eagle and the table ate an innocent Kookaburra.
review.summary: Round 1 was a muddle of rule misreads, but Farm still eggsecuted the Floofer. In round 2 Sphinx Alex was caught after his visit story shifted under an Eagle check. In round 3 the lone Meowfia, Mouser Casey, winked the Eagle. The table then piled onto a confused Kookaburra, and Farm lost. Finley won the game on round 2 points.

rounds.recap: Drew's Hawk claim wrongly named Blair as Meowfia. Blair was a Turkey, and that paid three visitors. Players misread the Turkey, Floofer and Falcon rules. Ellis's hug claim fit Casey's odd Owl report, and Ellis was eggsecuted as the Floofer.

Sphinx Alex claimed a visit to Casey that Blair's Eagle check contradicted. He then switched his story to Blair after the vote was called. Everyone threw at him, and Farm won. Finley, with a big throw of 8 and a 3 at the winning target, jumped to 22.

Casey, the only Meowfia, winked the Eagle Finley mid-day. Ellis was confused and lost 2 eggs, and he and Finley gave visit claims that did not match. The table locked onto Ellis, an innocent Farm player, and Meowfia won.

highlights.text: Casey and Ellis's hug claims lined up, which turned a messy Turkey pile-up into a clean catch of the Floofer.
Alex changed which player he visited right after the vote was called, and that gave the table its proof.
Casey winked the score leader Finley mid-day, and the lone Meowfia then steered the vote onto Ellis.
Confused Ellis reported a visit that contradicted the Eagle's report, and the table could not tell a real lie from a confusion.

confusions.what: Called Blair Meowfia from a Hawk egg that actually came from the Turkey's visitor payout.
First credited a Tit guess of Pigeon for his egg, then switched to the Turkey.
Said Floofer only hugs players who visit the Floofer, and misread the hug on Casey.
Said a Falcon's +2 had a second source he couldn't see, while the others doubted it. Blair, Ellis and Casey all said it didn't add up.
Said nobody visited the Turkey, though three players had.
Claimed Owl lays its egg in its own nest, and was corrected.
Said Alex's visit to the Eagle should have shown up, then corrected himself. The Eagle only learns visitors to its own target.
As Turkey, claimed nobody visited him, though a Turkey cannot see its visitors.
Read the confused report as a real visit contradiction and attacked Finley's Eagle claim with it.
Said someone visited him, though only Finley did.

worked: The Wink on the Mouser created a sharp Meowfia play in round 3: the winked Finley could not defend his Eagle report.
Cross-checking egg counts against claims (Turkey payouts, Eagle visitor checks) gave real evidence in rounds 1 and 2.
Throw-size signalling and keeping cards gave real decisions about how much to risk.
problems: Rule recall was poor. Turkey, Owl, Eagle and Floofer were misread repeatedly. Fix: give each player a short card text for their animal, or have the Storyteller correct plain misreads.
Confusion and hugs look like lies. Ellis's confused report and the round 1 hug were treated as contradictions. Fix: make the confusion effect clearer, or give a way to confirm it.
The round 3 Meowfia had too much power: a lone Mouser with a Wink won by killing the only checkable Eagle. Fix: reduce the Wink's effect or let a dead player's report stand.
Round 3 had only one Meowfia and no one else to contest the vote, so Farm bandwagoned on a weak case. Fix: add something to draw doubt, or require more than a lost egg count as evidence.
Scoring was lopsided. Finley led from round 1 and was never pressured, and a Farm loss still let him keep 23. Fix: add leader-catch-up pressure or a bigger swing for round 3.
